title: The Song of Moses and the Lamb

verses.text: Then I saw another great and marvelous sign in heaven: seven angels with the seven final plagues, with which the wrath of God is completed.
And I saw something like a sea of glass mixed with fire, beside which stood those who had conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name. They were holding harps from God,
and they sang the song of God's servant Moses and of the Lamb: "Great and wonderful are Your works, O Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations!
Who will not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy. All nations will come and worship before You, for Your righteous acts have been revealed."
After this I looked, and the temple—the tabernacle of the Testimony—was opened in heaven.
And out of the temple came the seven angels with the seven plagues, dressed in clean and bright linen and girded with golden sashes around their chests.
Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.
And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power; and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.

context.author: John, who was on the island of Patmos (1:1, 4, 9); traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Apocalypse, prophecy, and letter, full of symbols and visions
context.audience: Seven churches in the Roman province of Asia
context.setting: John sees another great and marvelous sign: seven angels with the seven last plagues. He sees those who conquered the beast standing beside a sea of glass mingled with fire, singing the song of Moses and the Lamb. The temple in heaven is opened, and the angels come out with the bowls of wrath.
context.custom: Singing on the shore recalls Israel after the Red Sea (Exodus 15). The phrase “the tabernacle of the Testimony” (v.5) means the tent of meeting of the wilderness years. Smoke filling the temple (v.8) echoes Exodus 40:34 and Isaiah 6:4, when God’s glory filled the sanctuary.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 16 pours out the seven bowls.
context.timelineBible: The song borrows from Exodus 15, Deuteronomy 32, and Psalms 86, 111, and 139. The plagues recall Egypt’s plagues. Leviticus 26:21 speaks of sevenfold punishment.

translation.meaning: Devout, faithful. A word used for God in the Greek Old Testament.

otBackground.note: All nations shall come and worship.
The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.

overview.summary: Those who conquered the beast sing the song of Moses and the Lamb beside a sea of glass, and seven angels receive the last plagues.

history.t: Moses and Israel sang after crossing the sea.

customs.t: The clothing of priests and the pure.

archaeology.t: Reconstruction of the tent of meeting.
The Oxford papyrus P115 includes parts of chapters 14 and 15, among the earliest witnesses to these verses.

overview.discussion: The song celebrates God’s justice and truth. Do I trust that God’s ways are just when I can’t see how things will work out?
overview.book: The book of Revelation · 22 chapters. A vision of Christ, judgment, and the new creation, written to encourage persecuted believers.
overview.author: John
